title: Dayasiri, Kumara Jayakody stage showdown in Parliament
summary: Opposition MP Dayasiri Jayasekera and former Minister of Power and Energy Kumara Jayakody engaged in a heated argument in Parliament on the issue of inferior quality coal.

title: SJB suspends Horana Organiser Charith Abeysinghe following bribery arrest
summary: The Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) has taken steps to suspend the party membership of its Horana Organiser, Charith Abeysinghe, following his arrest and subsequent remand over an alleged bribery incident.

title: Confiscated narcotics to be destroyed in Puttalam tomorrow
summary: A quantity of confiscated narcotics is scheduled to be destroyed tomorrow morning (June 27) at the incinerator facility located at Lactowatta in Wanathavilluwa, Puttalam.

title: Saudi Aramco resumes oil loading at Ras Tanura after 4-month halt
summary: Saudi Aramco resumed oil loading on Friday at its Ras Tanura terminal in the Gulf after a near four-month halt, shipping data from LSEG showed, in a sign ‌that Middle Eastern producers are pushing forward with plans to boost exports despite a ship attack in the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Warning over power bank fire risk on flights as summer holidays begin
summary: Flight passengers are being warned not to pack power banks or vapes in their hold luggage ahead of the busy summer holiday travel period beginning for parts of the UK.

title: Opposition MPs sign motion on judicial appointments delay
summary: Opposition MPs began signing a motion today to request for a special debate on the delay in appointing senior judicial officers.

title: President doesn't answer MPs’ phone calls: Dayasiri
summary: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake never answers MPs’ phone calls, Opposition MP Dayasiri Jayasekera told Parliament today.

title: Seven more battery energy storage systems arrive at Colombo Port
summary: A consignment of seven additional Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) arrived at the Colombo Port yesterday evening.

title: Afghanistan’s Taliban government imposes smartphone ban on government officials
summary: Afghanistan’s Taliban government has ordered a nationwide ban on civil servants’ smartphone use, a military court order showed, prompting warnings from rights activists that the move could further restrict access ‌to information.

title: Country loses US $ 1 billion in fraudulent transactions, certain banks involved
summary: In a shocking disclosure, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said in Parliament yesterday that the country had lost as much as US $ 1 billion because of the transfer of a whopping Rs.300 billion ill-gotten cash in terms of Telegraphic Transfers and Advanced Payments for imports. He said that certain banks had been implicated in the fraudulent transactions.

title: At least 40 injured in head-on bus collision in Matara
summary: At least 40 people have been hospitalized following a head-on collision between two private buses along the Matara-Talalla road, police said.

title: Philippines bans video game played by alleged high school shooter
summary: The Philippines has temporarily blocked gaming app Gorebox after an initial investigation found that a teenage suspect in a rare school shooting had been playing the game.

title: UN halts escort of ships through Hormuz after vessel comes under attack
summary: The U.N. International Maritime Organization paused its operation to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday after a vessel reported an attack, reigniting concerns about ‌whether a preliminary deal to end the Iran war will hold.

title: Chief Inspector arrested over death of female physiotherapist
summary: A Chief Inspector of Police has been arrested in connection with the death of a female physiotherapist found inside a car in Teldeniya.

title: Australia considers tougher enforcement of social media ban for teens
summary: Australia’s prime minister said on Friday he was keen to make sure the country’s social media ban ‌for children was as strong as possible, as a new study found that the measure — the first of its kind and now six months old — had little impact on teen use.
